acceptance_criteria: AC-1 (resolves council findings Security-D1 + Python-Architect-D2, both on section 3.2): section 3.2 gains two additions: (a) explicit handling for the MultiEdit tool -- state plainly that MultiEdit is NOT permitted against docs/design/po_drafts/*.md (Edit/Write only; a MultiEdit attempt falls through to the existing default-deny, exactly as it does for every other path today) since MultiEdit's tool_input is a list of {old_string,new_string} objects, not a single new_string, and the status-line regex has no defined behavior across multiple edit objects; (b) one explicit sentence recording that the Product Owner reviewed and accepted the status-line regex's residual bypass risk (a determined edit could evade `^\s*\*\*\s*(FROZEN|RATIFIED)\b` by omitting the bold marker or rephrasing) as an acceptable trade-off given the PO role is not modeled as an adversarial actor -- this is a written acceptance, not a stronger regex.

AC-2 (resolves Python-Architect-D1): section 3.1 gains one new acceptance-criterion line for GOV_PO_2_IMPLEMENTATION requiring the new gh pr diff/gh run view/gh run list prefix matches to be boundary-safe -- i.e. the matched prefix must be followed by a space or end-of-string, not merely `cmd.startswith(p)` unbounded, so a hypothetical colliding gh subcommand (e.g. a future `gh run viewer`) cannot slip through. State this as a required GOV_PO_2_IMPLEMENTATION acceptance criterion, not implemented in this amendment.

AC-3 (resolves Security-D2): section 3.1 gains one new prerequisite: before gh run view/gh run list ship, a one-time audit of .github/workflows/*.yml confirms no CI step echoes a secret or a CLASS-2+ identity value to stdout in a way GitHub Actions' own secret-masking would not catch -- perform this audit now, in this amendment movement (it is read-only, no code change), and record its result (pass/fail, and if fail, what must change first) directly in this section.

AC-4 (resolves DevSecOps-D1 + Python-Architect-D3, the same finding from two angles): section 3.4 gains one new required GOV_PO_2_IMPLEMENTATION acceptance criterion: a regression test that runs both main.py --repository-privacy-check and scripts/repository_privacy_check.py and asserts matching stdout (modulo the stated banner-line exception) and matching exit code, for at least one PASS case and one non-PASS gate value.

AC-5 (resolves DevSecOps-D2): section 5 gains one explicit sentence acknowledging that the bookkeeping-stays-with-the-engineer rule is accepted as policy-only (not gate-enforced) for now, despite the gate_3 precedent showing policy alone already failed twice before a dedicated backfill closed it -- name this explicitly as accepted risk rather than leaving it implicit, and note a structural convergence-test enforcement remains a legitimate future improvement not undertaken here.

AC-6 (resolves Technical-PO-D1): section 4 gains an explicit standing-delegation re-confirmation clause: each standing-delegation class named in section 4 must be re-affirmed by the Product Owner at the next relevant PLAN/REVIEW/DECIDE episode that actually uses it for the first time in a new context, or after any six-month gap, whichever comes first -- a single use outside a class's plain-language description reverts to the unnamed section 6.3/D2 restatement path (no standing delegation applies) until re-affirmed.

AC-7 (resolves Technical-PO-D2, light touch): section 1 gains one clarifying sentence: sections 3.4 (privacy-check script) and 3.5 (evidence-reviewer agent) are enabling mechanisms subordinate to seams 1 and 2 respectively, not independently-justified new scope beyond the three named seams -- so the document's own proportionality claim is accurate rather than implicit.
